globalBoundaries: Use the XLSX only as evidence for table structure, metric organization, and formatting tendencies.
Do not infer missing business meaning, hidden sheets, formulas, units, or print settings from absent evidence.
Do not promise Excel export, exact visual recreation, high-fidelity restoration, or source-document reconstruction.
Rules may provide fallback behavior when evidence is absent, but such fallbacks must remain conservative and diagnostic-friendly.
rationale: Evidence supports a single-sheet, compact metric table with limited style diversity; detailed rules are conservative and executable but avoid unsupported visual claims.

attributes.name: sheetName
attributes.value: Sheet1

rules.detail: Build formatting logic around one detected worksheet and one compact used range. Do not split the content into multiple independent documents unless later evidence shows additional sheets or regions.
rules.rule: Treat the workbook as a single top-level tabular document container.

rules.detail: Any downstream representation should preserve table logic and cite uncertainty where required rather than claiming a generated workbook deliverable.
rules.rule: The workbook is a reference source for structure and metrics, not a requested finished spreadsheet artifact.

attributes.name: sheetName
attributes.value: Sheet1

rules.detail: If a display title is needed, derive it from user instructions or verified cell content outside this evidence pack. The sheet label alone must not create a business topic.
rules.rule: Use the worksheet name only as a locator, not as a semantic title.

attributes.name: printLayout
attributes.value: fit-used-range-one-table-per-page-if-printing-is-requested

rules.detail: The active table canvas is columns A through C and rows 1 through 29. Empty surrounding cells should remain outside the formatting target.
rules.rule: Constrain formatting operations to the detected used range unless new evidence expands it.

attributes.name: headerRow
attributes.value: 1 or first content row after title detection

attributes.name: dataRegion
attributes.value: A2:C29 unless title/header analysis changes boundary

rules.detail: Because only range-level evidence is available, row 1 should be treated as a header/title candidate; rows below it form the initial data-region candidate until cell-level content proves a different split.
rules.rule: Partition the used range into title/header candidates, data body, and possible summary or note rows by row role.

attributes.name: headerRow
attributes.value: candidate row 1

attributes.name: fontSizePt
attributes.value: data-size plus 0 to 1 pt, capped by available style evidence

rules.detail: Use one consistent header style across the detected three-column region. If a separate title row is later confirmed, keep title styling distinct from field-header styling.
rules.rule: Render header cells as short field labels with stronger emphasis than data cells.

attributes.name: columnWidth
attributes.value: auto-fit within A:C; prefer wrap over adding columns

rules.detail: For a compact indicator table, header alignment should support column scanning. Text wrapping is allowed for long field labels rather than widening the table beyond the detected three-column layout.
rules.rule: Align header labels centrally within their cells unless column content requires a measured exception.

attributes.name: dataRegion
attributes.value: body rows inside A1:C29 after header/title detection

rules.detail: Do not flatten metric rows into prose-only paragraphs. Each observation must remain traceable to its row and column position within the table region.
rules.rule: Preserve row-column relationships as the primary meaning carrier.

attributes.name: tableRegion
attributes.value: 29 rows by 3 columns

attributes.name: columnWidth
attributes.value: auto-fit each of A:C to content with consistent minimum width

rules.detail: Row height, wrapping, and padding should prioritize complete visibility and scanability. Avoid oversized decorative spacing that would obscure the compact metric-table character.
rules.rule: Use compact table density suitable for 29 rows and 3 columns.

attributes.name: fill
attributes.value: reuse no more than the detected small fill family unless explicitly specified

attributes.name: border
attributes.value: reuse a limited border family; avoid decorative border proliferation

rules.detail: The detected workbook has limited font, fill, border, and cell-style counts. Maintain that restraint: title, header, body, and optional note/summary styles are sufficient unless content evidence requires more.
rules.rule: Use a small, controlled style set rather than many ad hoc variants.

attributes.name: tableRegion
attributes.value: A1:C29 includes merged-cell evidence

rules.detail: Merged areas should not be duplicated into every covered cell. Read and render the merged value once at the merged region's logical anchor.
rules.rule: Treat merged cells as layout signals that may mark titles, group labels, or notes.

attributes.name: numberFormat
attributes.value: preserve detected literal values; no formula-derived recalculation

rules.detail: If totals, ratios, or derived indicators are needed later, mark them as newly derived and keep them separate from imported cell facts.
rules.rule: Do not infer calculated fields or formulas where no formula evidence is detected.

attributes.name: numberFormat
attributes.value: preserve-source-display-or-general-when-undetected

attributes.name: unit
attributes.value: not detected; require explicit evidence before applying

rules.detail: When a cell is numeric, retain its apparent precision and sign style. Percent, currency, date, or unit labels may be applied only when present in verified cell formatting or user instructions.
rules.rule: Preserve detected numeric display semantics and avoid inventing units.

attributes.name: border
attributes.value: consistent inner grid; stronger header separator if role detected

rules.detail: Apply consistent inner gridlines to the data body and slightly stronger separation for header or summary rows when identified. Border variety should remain within the small detected style family.
rules.rule: Use borders to clarify the compact grid without turning the table into a decorative layout.

attributes.name: fill
attributes.value: limited structural fills; no invented heatmap coloring

rules.detail: Because only a small fill set is detected, avoid alternating or multi-color semantic encodings unless cell-level evidence later confirms them.
rules.rule: Use fill color only for structural emphasis such as header, title, or summary rows.

attributes.name: printLayout
attributes.value: print-area=A1:C29; orientation=undetected; fit-width=1-page-if-needed

rules.detail: Set print area to the detected used range, preserve portrait or landscape choice as unknown until explicit evidence appears, and prefer scaling that keeps all three columns visible.
rules.rule: If print layout is requested, fit the used table region as one compact report area.

attributes.name: unit
attributes.value: unknown unless present in verified cells or user instructions

attributes.name: printLayout
attributes.value: unknown except used-range fit policy when requested

rules.detail: Do not assert exact font names, exact column widths, exact colors, formulas, units, print orientation, or hidden semantic groupings from this evidence pack alone.
rules.rule: Unobserved formatting details must remain unspecified or marked as inferred defaults.
